articles.title: Nandy 'minded to intervene' in Sky's £1.6bn takeover of ITV entertainment arm
articles.summary: The culture secretary says the deal could affect free expression in the media and the variety of Britain's news landscape.
articles.body:
Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy has said she is "minded to intervene" in the proposed £1.6bn deal for Sky to buy ITV's media and entertainment division.

Nandy said there were reasonable grounds to believe the deal could affect free expression in the media and the variety of Britain's news landscape.

Sky said it would "carefully consider" a letter from the culture secretary and "engage constructively" with the review into the deal.

"We remain confident that bringing Sky and ITV's media and entertainment business together will create a stronger British media," it said.

ITV welcomed the letter and said the deal would help it "compete with global streaming platforms, benefiting viewers, advertisers and the UK creative industries".

The two companies announced in July that Sky had agreed to buy ITV's broadcasting business, including its free-to-air TV channels and the ITV X streaming service.

The deal does not include ITV's production arm, ITV Studios, which makes popular programmes such as Love Island and I'm a Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here.

It would give Sky access to millions more viewers, while bosses hope it would help both compete with streaming giants such as Netflix.

What Sky buying ITV could mean for your favourite shows

But Nandy has told Sky and ITV that she is considering issuing a public interest intervention notice (PIIN) to the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) and regulator Ofcom, forcing an investigation into the tie-up.

In a letter to both companies, she said she was minded to order the probe to address public interest considerations including:

The need for free expression of opinion in news media

The need for a range of views in news media across the UK

The need for a range of people controlling the media across the UK

The need for a wide range of programmes to be offered across the UK

The letter said Nandy recognised Sky News and ITV News were two of the most prominent sources of television news in the UK, with a joint 26% share of those viewing news on linear TV.

Consumers would still have access to other sources of news such as the BBC and Channel 4, it added.

But Nandy believes that, over time, the tie-up could undermine the range of views available to viewers, with 86% of the linear TV news market controlled by the BBC and Sky/ITV.

The North of England could be particularly hard hit as well as nations of the UK other than England and those from lower socio-economic backgrounds, the letter argued.

This is because their main source of news is broadcast news, it added.

Sky and ITV have been given until 20 October to respond to the culture secretary's concerns.

A Sky spokesperson said: "We have already made clear commitments to protect ITV's identity, its free-to-air services and public service broadcasting obligations, and to ensure ITV News and Sky News remain distinct editorial voices."

An ITV spokesperson said: "We welcome the publication of the secretary of state's 'minded to' issue a public interest intervention notice letter as was expected and look forward to fully co-operating in the process.

"This is another important milestone in the regulatory review process towards creating a UK player with the scale and resources to better compete with global streaming platforms, benefiting viewers, advertisers and the UK creative industries."

Nandy's intervention would be made under a new public interest consideration.

This would need legislation to be brought forward, given that current laws do not cover the effect of a merger on streaming or on-demand programmes.

She said: "If I decide to intervene on the basis of this new public interest consideration, I will bring forward legislation... to extend the application of the public interest consideration relating to the availability of a wide range of broadcasting to on-demand programmes."

articles.title: Another man admits raping woman drugged and abused by husband
articles.summary: The husband is accused of inviting 13 other men to abuse her at their family home in Stockport.
articles.body:
Another man has pleaded guilty to raping a woman who was drugged and abused by her husband without her knowledge for over 20 years.

Graham Brougham, 74, is the oldest of 13 men who were charged with sexual offences against the victim after being allegedly invited into her home, in the Stockport area of Greater Manchester, to abuse her by her husband.

The husband, in his sixties, has already admitted 62 offences against his wife - including rape - and has given a witness statement detailing "what he says happened".

Brougham, from Northwich, was told by a judge at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court that he "should be under no illusion his sentence will be custody and a long time in custody."

The victim, who held hands with a family member, watched on from the public gallery as Brougham answered "guilty" in the dock to a charge of raping her in September 2024.

The husband, who remains in custody, cannot be identified to protect the anonymity of his wife.

Two other men, 59-year-old Keith Fotheringham from Dundee, Scotland; and Sean Peers, 38, from Stockport, had already admitted sexually abusing her at previous hearings.

The trial of 10 other defendants accused of sexual offences against the victim has been delayed until 2 November for legal and practical reasons.

They are all alleged to have committed offences against the same victim between 2015 and November 2025.

Brougham was released on conditional bail and will be sentenced at the conclusion of the trial of his co-defendants.

Earlier this month, the nine women and three men of the jury, plus two female reserve jurors, were told that the husband had provided a witness statement detailing "what it is he says happened" after his guilty pleas.

Judge Maurice Greene said: "That statement is a long statement and that has been disclosed to all defence counsel and it contains a lot of detail."

The judge said the statement contained "lots of pages and lots of documents" and that lawyers in the case were "going through it carefully", which was ongoing work.

articles.title: Chats from Nolan Wells' phone show what friends said when he vanished
articles.summary: Messages pulled from Nolan Wells​' phone show what his friends said before and after the 18-year-old disappeared in early July following a boat outing with f...
articles.body:
Group chats pulled from Nolan Wells ' cellphone show what his friends said before and after the Mississippi teen vanished in early July following a boat outing with friends.

Wells disappeared after he and a group of friends celebrated the Fourth of July holiday off the Gulf Coast. They say he left his phone on their boat but didn't return with them.

A nearly 300-page report analyzing the late teen's phone and recently uploaded on the Justice for Nolan Wells website reveals his friends' reactions to his disappearance and speculation about his death in dozens of group chats.

On July 5, one group chat discusses when Wells was last seen, saying, "He got off our boat with this other guy and they started walking back to their boat." Minutes later, one friend calls it suspicious, saying, "There is def some sus s*** going on."

At one point, they talked about trying to find Wells, asking everyone to check their camera rolls. Another user added, "See if he was talking to anyone we don't know."

Another message read: "That's not like Nolan bro just to get left."

Someone else writes, "Hes gotta be shlumped somewhere rn hopefully." Another answers: "It's already noon though," followed by, "He might've got drugged or something."

Wells' body was recovered in the waters off Horn Island two days later. Once news broke of his death, one friend messaged: "Nolan was the most nice and caring guy we knew."

The day after his disappearance, the group appeared frustrated with the national headlines, writing: "All i keep seeing is white folk made it home and the one black kid didn't." Another answered: "It ain't ever been like that with us bro."

Last month, Jackson County's district attorney announced a Mississippi grand jury found no criminal wrongdoing in Wells' death.

Legal analyst Jessica Levinson told CBS News there is nothing in the recently released report that would change the DA's conclusion that there is no evidence of a crime.

Wells' parents spoke to CBS News in July, with his father Elmore Wonsley saying he didn't believe his son decided to stay on the island by himself. "It just doesn't — that's not his character," he said.

articles.title: 'Stunned': Rahul urges President Murmu to put Dushyant Gautam’s appointment as Sikkim Governor on hold
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi has written to President Droupadi Murmu, urging her to reconsider Dushyant Gautam’s
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi has written to President Droupadi Murmu, urging her to reconsider Dushyant Gautam’s appointment as Sikkim Governor amid renewed demands for justice in the 2022 Ankita Bhandari murder case. The move comes as Ankita’s parents warn of nationwide protests if the appointment is not revoked.In a letter shared alongside a post on X, Gandhi said the identity of the alleged VIP mentioned in the case remained unresolved nearly four years after of 19-year-old Bhandari’s murder. He alleged that the investigation into the VIP angle was proceeding slowly and questioned Gautam’s appointment while the inquiry remained pending.“Madam President, 19-year-old Ankita Bhandari refused to compromise her dignity for a VIP, which led to her murder. Even four years later, due to the CBI's sluggish investigation, the question remains: who was that VIP?” Gandhi wrote on X.He added that many people, including Bhandari’s family, believed Gautam was connected to the case. These remain allegations, and Gautam’s alleged links to the crime have not been established in the information provided.In his letter, Rahul argued that a Governor’s constitutional position could complicate any future criminal proceedings. He cited Article 74(1) of the Constitution, saying the President could ask the government to reconsider its advice.“I request you to ask the Government to reconsider this appointment, and that Mr. Gautam not take office until the CBI has completed its investigation,” he wrote.Rahul also referred to the family’s continuing demand for justice, saying, “Ankita refused the repellent demand made of her and paid with her life. Her parents, who are still fighting for justice, are now protesting this appointment and being detained by police. Please act-provide solace to Ankita's grieving parents and protect the high post of Governor.”He also criticised Prime Minister Narendra Modi over the appointment. “While serving as Governor, no criminal proceedings can be initiated against him. By advising the appointment of Dushyant Gautam, Prime Minister Modi has proven that he has absolutely no concern for women's safety. I appeal to you to advise the government to reconsider this appointment and not allow Dushyant Gautam to assume office until the investigation is complete. Do not let the hope for justice of Ankita's parents be shattered", Rahul wrote.Ankita’s parents issue 24-hour ultimatumRahul’s letter comes a day after he met Bhandari’s parents at India Gate in Delhi, where they were protesting against Gautam’s appointment. On Thursday, Delhi Police briefly detained the family and several Opposition leaders during a sit-in at Delhi's India Gate.Bhandari’s father, Virendra Singh Bhandari, issued a 24-hour ultimatum to the government, warning of nationwide protests if the appointment was not revoked.“We are giving the government a 24-hour ultimatum. If it does not revoke Dushyant Gautam’s appointment, people across the country, in every state, will take to the streets to demand justice for Ankita Bhandari,” he told IANS.Bhandari, who worked as a receptionist at the Vanantra resort near Rishikesh, was murdered on September 18, 2022. Resort owner Pulkit Arya and two employees were convicted and sentenced to life imprisonment. The alleged VIP angle has remained a focus of the family’s demands, and the CBI inquiry into it is ongoing.Rahul's appeal now places the President’s response and the government’s position on Gautam’s appointment under scrutiny, as the family presses for the investigation to be completed before he assumes the constitutional post.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Boiling point’: Why students are protesting against Albania’s Edi Rama
articles.summary: Experts say Albania’s protests reflect ignored student grievances and growing frustration.
articles.body:
Student protests against poor conditions in Albania’s education system have continued for a third day in the capital, Tirana, as Prime Minister Edi Rama insists he will not resign.

Demonstrators have called on Rama to quit in often violent protests since Tuesday. They have set fire to several buildings across the city, including the prime minister’s office, ministry buildings and branches of several banks.

Dozens of police officers and protesters have been injured amid attempts to disperse the crowds using water cannon and tear gas.

“What you are seeing is the boiling point of months of suppressed grievances,” Albanian journalist Arlis Alikaj told Al Jazeera.

Students have complained for months about the high cost of education and their limited employment prospects after graduation.

Afrim Krasniqi, a professor and researcher at the Institute for Political Studies in Tirana, told Al Jazeera that students and young people protested peacefully for nearly three months, “yet their demands were largely ignored, while the government often responded with discrediting campaigns rather than genuine dialogue”.

He added that the current escalation reflects “frustration not only with the government itself, but also with the lack of institutional accountability and responsiveness.”

The protests represent one of the most serious waves of public discontent directed at Rama, who won a fourth term last May but has since faced public anger over corruption allegations involving senior officials.

The unrest in Tirana coincides with a broader wave of student protests across Europe. In France, secondary school students have spent weeks protesting and blockading schools, demanding more teachers and better learning facilities. They have warned that deteriorating school buildings and overcrowded classrooms are undermining the quality of education.

Protests against Rama’s government began a few months ago, fuelled by plans to build a luxury resort along Albania’s largely unspoilt southern coast. Jared Kushner , US President Donald Trump’s son in law, is involved in the project.

Local media reported that the protests spread from Tirana to universities in Elbasan and Shkoder on Wednesday.

Albania is among the economies of the Western Balkans seeking to catch up with European living standards. However, the gap with the European Union average remains evident in purchasing power, wages, productivity and the quality of public services. Despite economic progress, the country continues to face challenges including emigration, regional inequalities and the need for stronger institutions and the rule of law.

After Montenegro, Albania stands out as one of the countries that has made the most progress towards full EU membership. However, behind the optimistic political rhetoric, frustration is growing among citizens over the slow pace of European integration and the lack of tangible improvements in their daily lives.

While opposition groups seek to support the demonstrators and capitalise on the moment to strengthen their own position, Alikaj said the protests are being driven by young people and students demanding systemic change.

On Thursday, Rama – who has been PM since 2013 – told Reuters, “As for calls for my resignation, governments change through democratic elections. Last year, we had elections, not a revolution.”

Sokol Lleshi, a lecturer at the University of New York Tirana specialising in political science and international relations, said social change is more likely to emerge from a broader coalition of different social groups, rather than mass mobilisation limited to university and secondary school students.

“Elite defection from the current ruling political elite could enable the institutional means to channel societal dissatisfaction or resentment into political and policy changes. Yet, the current student protest does not seem to replicate the December 2018 mass movement of university students and its effects”, Lleshi said.

The student protests that shook Albania in December 2018 began over rising education costs and forced Rama to dismiss eight ministers as part of a cabinet reshuffle and announce a package of measures known as the “Pact for the University”.

But some of the students’ demands remained unmet.

Lleshi drew some more positive conclusions from Albania’s past experience of social unrest.

Albanian society is polarised and unequal, “with hollowed intermediary political institutions”, he said, but the legacy of unrest and political confrontation will serve as a “warning to avoid destabilisation”, he said.

articles.title: A 10-year-old Jack Russell terrier escaped a Yellowstone cabin and survived 34 days in the park; rescuers trapped her just before winter ended the search after she lost about 10 pounds, nearly half her weight
articles.summary: Luna, a 10-year-old Jack Russell terrier, has been found alive after spending 34 days loose in Yellowstone National Park.
articles.body: Luna, a 10-year-old Jack Russell terrier, has been found alive after spending 34 days loose in Yellowstone National Park. The small dog escaped from her family’s rented cabin on September 10 while they were visiting the park. Rescuers finally found her on October 14, just as the approaching winter threatened to bring the search to a halt. Luna was taken directly to a veterinarian for treatment after losing about 10 pounds from her original weight of 18 pounds.According to a report by 'Cowboy State Daily', Katie Boucher, president of the Norris Arc Training and Recovery Center, led the search. Luna had been spotted dozens of times around the Canyon Village area, but catching her proved difficult. With search permits nearing expiry and winter conditions approaching, the rescue team had only a few days left to find her before suspending operations.How Luna escaped from her cabinLuna was on holiday in Yellowstone with her family from California when she disappeared. On September 10, her owners left her inside their rented cabin in the Canyon Village area while they went to Norris Geyser Basin, where dogs are not permitted. A “Do Not Disturb” sign had been placed on the door, but housekeeping staff apparently entered the room by mistake. Luna slipped outside and ran away. Her family spent the first week searching for her themselves before seeking help from Boucher and her team. Although Luna was repeatedly seen around the park, she remained difficult to approach or capture.Boucher said Luna’s early life may help explain her ability to survive alone. The dog had lived as a street dog during the first year of her life before being rescued and adopted. After escaping, she appeared to fall back on those survival instincts, avoiding people rather than seeking help. “She has street skills,” Boucher had previously told *Cowboy State Daily*. “She knows how to survive.” Luna’s repeated sightings kept hope alive, but the search was becoming increasingly urgent. Boucher’s permits were due to expire on Monday, while the park’s winter shutdown was expected at the end of October. The team feared that falling temperatures and worsening weather would make it unsafe to continue searching.The trap that finally brought Luna to safetyBoucher narrowed down the area where Luna appeared to be sleeping each night and set up a humane Missy trap. The enclosure was equipped with shelter and items carrying familiar scents to encourage the dog to enter. The trap could be monitored remotely and closed once Luna was safely inside. The breakthrough came on Wednesday morning, October 14. Boucher’s team had placed a small doghouse inside the trap to give Luna shelter during a storm. When the rescuers returned to reset the trap and continue their efforts, they found the terrier inside the doghouse.“We put a small doghouse in there for shelter during the storm,” Boucher told Cowboy State Daily. “This morning, when we went to reset it and resume our trapping efforts, she was in the doghouse waiting for us.” Luna’s owners, who had returned from California earlier to help with scent-trail efforts, were the first to reach the trap and find her. Boucher arrived soon afterwards. “The feeling never gets old,” she said. “Pure joy.” After more than a month of uncertainty, the reunion marked the end of an exhausting search that had drawn attention from people in and around the national park. The rescuers had been racing against a seasonal deadline, and Luna’s capture meant they would not have to abandon the effort and return in the spring.Luna is taken to a veterinarianLuna was taken straight to a veterinarian after being found. As of Wednesday afternoon, she was still receiving medical attention, and Boucher said she was waiting to learn more about the dog’s condition. At that point, she did not know whether Luna would need to stay overnight. The weight loss was significant. Luna weighed 18 pounds when she escaped and had lost about 10 pounds during her time alone, leaving her roughly 8 pounds. That represents a loss of more than half her original body weight, making veterinary assessment especially important after her prolonged time outdoors.The precise extent of her condition had not yet been confirmed when *Cowboy State Daily* published its report. While the successful capture brought relief to her family and rescuers, Luna still needed professional care after her ordeal. Her survival in Yellowstone’s wilderness, followed by her safe capture just before the winter search deadline, brought a hopeful conclusion to a month-long effort. For the rescuers who continued looking despite repeated setbacks, the moment they found Luna waiting inside the doghouse was the news they had worked so hard to deliver.Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates. articles.title: 'Victims' families may witness in person': US not to livestream execution of Fort Hood gunman Nidal Hasan
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump announced on Thursday that the execution of Fort Hood gunman Nidal Hasan would not be livestreamed, but the victims’ immediate
articles.body: US President Donald Trump announced on Thursday that the execution of Fort Hood gunman Nidal Hasan would not be livestreamed, but the victims’ immediate family members would be allowed to witness it in person if they chose to do so.“He (Hasan) will die, as scheduled, by firing squad, but this event will not be livestreamed. The execution may be witnessed in person by the immediate families of the victims, if they so choose. They deserve to witness JUSTICE!” Trump posted on his Truth Social platform, referring to the November 5, 2009, shooting at the US Army’s Fort Hood base in Texas.Former US Army Major Hasan is scheduled to be executed by firing squad on December 3. Trump described him as a “very bad and evil man” in his post.“Nidal Malik Hasan is a very bad and evil man, who killed 13 people, including a pregnant soldier, who died, along with her unborn son, and injured, very seriously, 32 more innocent people,” Trump wrote.“With all of that being said, I think streaming the execution for all to see might have been a strong deterrent for the World to witness how America deals with Terrorists and SCUM like Hasan but, many very good and well meaning people would not rather watch die, through streaming, or through any other visual device,” he added.US defence secretary Pete Hegseth had announced earlier this month that Hasan’s execution would be public. Subsequent confirmation from the Pentagon that it would be livestreamed drew significant backlash from both Republicans and Democrats, with critics warning that the footage could be used to fuel radicalisation.What happened at Fort HoodHasan, an Army psychiatrist who held the rank of major, walked into a medical building on November 5, 2009, where soldiers were waiting in long lines to receive immunisations and medical clearance for deployment. He opened fire with a laser-sighted handgun. He also shot at the backs of soldiers fleeing toward the parking lot.Hasan claimed it was an effort to stop them from going to Afghanistan, where he would have to kill his fellow Muslims. A military judge barred him from presenting that as a defence during his 2013 trial. Hasan was left paralysed from the waist down after being shot in the back by law enforcement, and he now uses a wheelchair.Hasan could seek a lengthy delay of his execution, though given his behaviour at trial, he may not want to.The US military hasn’t executed a service member by firing squad since World War II. The last US service member was executed on April 13, 1961, when Army Pvt. John Bennett was executed by hanging.(With AP inputs)You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Newcastle Mercury Prize Fringe events to show off 'phenomenal' scene
articles.summary: Musician Tom A. Smith says the North East is the "cultural hub" of the country.
articles.body:
North-east England feels like the centre of the music scene ahead of the Mercury Prize, a musician has said.

The first event of the Mercury Prize Fringe is to begin later, kickstarting a week-long programme of performances, workshops and talks across Tyneside.

It is the prestigious music award's second year in Newcastle , with Geordie Sam Fender taking home the prize in 2025 for his album People Watching.

Tom A. Smith, from Sunderland, will headline BBC Introducing Live at the Glasshouse on Monday and said Fender's success had "inspired a generation of bands" in the region.

Smith said he hoped the festival would give people a chance to see Newcastle's music scene for what it is.

"The North East is just so phenomenal, it feels like the cultural hub in the country in terms of music right now.

"I'm lucky and I'm fortunate that I can travel around the country and different places and experience the music scene in so many different areas and it doesn't feel as exciting as the North East does right now."

Smith puts a lot of the buzz down to Sam Fender's recent success.

"He feels like he is the sort of figurehead of guitar music in a sense at the moment and I think it's carrying through the whole of the North East," he said.

"It's just totally inspired a generation of bands that are almost like the New Wave across the country."

Led by music development agency Generator, the fringe events aim to showcase Newcastle's music scene and create opportunities for emerging talent.

Events include a Mini Mercury for musicians aged 12-18 on Sunday, giving the younger generation a chance to take over a professional music venue.

On Tuesday, local nominated band Knats will return to the West End for a listening party and conversation discussing the stories behind their shortlisted album.

But Knats' A Great Day in Newcastle is not the only local nomination.

South Shields' Jade is shortlisted for her album That's Showbiz Baby!, and so will take on the likes of Olivia Dean, Raye and Paul McCartney.

The winner will be announced at a ceremony at the Utilita Arena on 22 October.

articles.summary: MEERUT: Convicts Muskan Rastogi and Sahil Shukla spent a restless first night in jail after a Meerut court sentenced them to death for murdering Muskan’s
articles.body: MEERUT: Convicts Muskan Rastogi and Sahil Shukla spent a restless first night in jail after a Meerut court sentenced them to death for murdering Muskan’s husband, merchant navy officer Saurabh Rajput.Both skipped dinner and remained distressed, jail sources said on Thursday.Muskan reportedly sat in a corner of the barrack, holding her 10-month-old daughter Radha, and cried until late at night, news agency PTI reported.Jail authorities have stepped up security and arranged regular medical examinations and counselling for the convicts.Muskan and Sahil are also preparing to challenge the death sentence in the Allahabad high court.District jail senior superintendent Viresh Raj Sharma said both convicts broke down after the verdict on Wednesday. They were counselled and informed about the next steps in the legal process.Sahil has been allotted prisoner number 395/2026 and Muskan 396/2026. Sahil has been shifted to a barrack for male convicts, while Muskan remains in the women’s barrack with her infant daughter, Sharma said.He added that doctors and jail officials had been directed to monitor their health.Counselling sessions were held on Wednesday evening and Thursday morning, PTI reported.Prisoners sentenced to death could take two to four days to recover from the immediate emotional impact of the verdict, he said.Both convicts have expressed their intention to appeal, Sharma said. They are expected to inform the jail administration within two to three days whether they will engage private lawyers or seek legal representation through the prison authorities.If their families or private lawyers do not file an appeal, the jail administration will approach the high court within 30 days, he said.Government lawyer Rekha Jain also said the sentence would be challenged, PTI reported.Muskan seeks meeting with elder daughterMuskan has been seeking permission to meet her seven-year-old daughter, Pihu.She was told that the child would have to be brought to the jail. Muskan had also sought permission to write a letter to her daughter. Although permission was granted, she had not submitted the letter by Thursday.Radha continues to stay with Muskan in prison. Under jail rules, children can remain with their incarcerated mothers until the age of six, PTI reported.Saurabh’s mother, Renu Devi, said the family did not wish to adopt Radha. She said the family was satisfied with the court’s verdict and did not wish to maintain any relationship with the infant.However, Renu Devi said the family was willing to take care of Pihu if her maternal grandparents agreed to send her.Sharma said Sahil had opted for farming and gardening work in jail, while Muskan had chosen stitching and embroidery. Neither participated in the programmes organised during Navratri.Court describes murder as extremely cruelA Meerut court on Wednesday sentenced Muskan and Sahil to death for the murder.District judge Arvind Kumar Mishra described the crime as extremely cruel and grave, according to the prosecution.Saurabh was killed on March 3, 2025. His body was dismembered and the remains placed inside a blue drum filled with cement. The crime came to light about a fortnight later, PTI reported.The court convicted Muskan and Sahil on September 30 after a 13-month trial involving 126 hearings.The prosecution examined 22 witnesses, including people linked to the purchase of the drum and other materials allegedly used in the crime.Hotel managers and cab drivers were also examined to establish the accused’s movements.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Meerut | Silver Rate in Meerut | Bank Holidays in Meerut | Public Holidays in Meerut | Meerut AQI | Weather in Meerut | Petrol Price in Meerut | Diesel Price in Meerut | CNG Price in Meerut | LPG Price in MeerutStay updated with the latest Meerut news. articles.title: German court sentences two for plotting to kill leader of Jewish community for Iran
articles.summary: A German court on Thursday handed two men prison sentences of up to 8-1/2 years for planning to kill the leader of a Jewish organization in Germany, saying one man had been steered by Iran’s intelligence service.
articles.body: FRANKFURT, Germany — A German court on Thursday handed two men prison sentences of up to 8-1/2 years for planning to kill the leader of a Jewish organization in Germany, saying one man had been steered by Iran’s intelligence service. One man, previously identified as Danish national Ali S., was sentenced to eight years and six months for preparing an assassination and aggravated arson, judges ruled. “The court is convinced that the defendant, S., was recruited by the Iranian secret service and integrated into it to carry out state-sponsored terrorist activities in Germany under Iran’s direction,” the court in the northern city of Hamburg said in a statement. The Iranian Embassy in Germany did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Another man, previously named as Afghan national Tawab M., was sentenced to four years and six months for his role in the plot. The verdicts, which can be appealed, come as a war with Iran launched by the United States and Israel in February has spilled over into an escalating conflict between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis. German federal prosecutors brought criminal charges against the two men in May. The court said that in early 2025, S. was tasked with gathering information on the President of the Central Council of Jews in Germany, Josef Schuster, and the Chairman of the German-Israeli Society, Volker Beck. He was also instructed to spy on two Jewish grocers in Berlin, they added.

articles.title: Sexual assault reported at fraternity house near University of Chicago
articles.summary: A person of interest has been identified after a 21-year-old woman told police that she was sexually assaulted at a fraternity party near the University of Chicago last weekend, amid national outrage over sexual misconduct on college campuses.
articles.body: A person of interest has been identified after a 21-year-old woman told police that she was sexually assaulted at a fraternity party near the University of Chicago last weekend, amid national outrage over sexual misconduct on college campuses. Neither the woman nor the person of interest is a student, according to the university. It said it was “not at liberty to disclose” his name, but that he has been banned from the campus. The University of Chicago said in a series of press releases this week that the woman told police the incident occurred at a party held at the Alpha Epsilon Pi fraternity house, just off of campus. She made the report in the early hours of Sunday, the university said. The New York Times interviewed one woman, Mia Lara, a 21-year-old student at a nearby university, who said she witnessed her friend sitting on the floor, slumped against the wall with her clothes and undergarments pulled down. She told the Times her friend began saying, “Make it stop” and “Get me out of here.” Lara told the Times she began screaming and the man fled. Lara chased the man in a video that’s gone viral on TikTok this week, where she can be seen accusing him of assaulting her friend in the bathroom at the fraternity party. “She wanted to,” the man replies as he runs off. “This is deeply concerning for the University community,” the school said in a statement. “The safety and well-being of our students and all who come to our community is our highest priority.” The Chicago Police Department said no arrests have been made and that no further information was available. The university said the woman was taken to the University of Chicago Medical Center and that university police immediately contacted the Chicago Police Department. The university noted that fraternities are not “Recognized Student Organizations” at UChicago and therefore have no formal affiliation with the school. It added that “all University students are subject to University policies and disciplinary procedures” and that it “remains committed to addressing sexual misconduct cases.” In a statement Tuesday, Alpha Epsilon Pi’s Lambda chapter said the “perpetrator” was chased out of the house and that members are cooperating with authorities. The chapter said it learned of the “situation” from one of the party’s “sober monitors,” and that members immediately helped the woman. “A member stayed with the victim until the necessary authorities arrived, only leaving after the police had asked him to do so,” the fraternity said. “The party was shut down immediately following our notice of the events.” “We will continue to support the investigation to the fullest extent and offer our support in any way possible,” the fraternity added. The Chicago Sun-Times, citing a police report, reported Tuesday that several men at the party blocked the woman’s friends from entering a bathroom, where she was found “not fully conscious” or clothed. The newspaper added that at least one of the men got into a physical altercation with one of the woman’s friends, according to the report. NBC News has not independently obtained the report. The Chicago Police Department declined to provide a copy. The fraternity’s national organization said in a statement that its members have a “responsibility to protect each other, our guests, and our community at all times.” University of Chicago student Alexa Walsh told NBC Chicago she hopes the university and fraternity take the allegation “seriously.” “To hear that a woman came to our campus just trying to have some fun and was sexually assaulted is very, very upsetting,” she said. The UChicago allegation comes amid national furor over a former Cornell University student’s allegation that she was gang-raped at an off-campus fraternity house in 2024. The woman, identified in court documents as Jane Doe, sued the university, the fraternity, Chi Phi, her sorority, Tri Delta, and seven former Chi Phi members last month in connection with the incident. After facing weeks of sharp criticism, Cornell said Tuesday it is suspending all “parties and social events” at fraternity houses for the rest of the academic year.

articles.title: Belfast Harbour: £15m into zero-emission transport testing project
articles.summary: It comes after a £15m investment from UK Research and Innovation's Local Innovation Partnerships Fund.
articles.body:
Belfast Harbour is to become a live environment for testing zero-emission transport and energy systems.

It comes after a £15m investment from UK Research and Innovation's Local Innovation Partnerships Fund.

The cluster led by Artemis Technologies, will connect electric vessels, high-power marine charging, autonomous transport and energy systems through secure digital twin technology.

Testing these technologies in an operational port will show how they work as an integrated system and help reduce barriers to commercial adoption.

Artemis Technologies CEO Dr Iain Percy said they are creating a digital network that will allow them to "optimise" both transport and energy use.

"What does that mean for most people? It means your bus turns up at the right time in terms of transport.

"But in terms of energy it means, more significantly that when the wind is blowing too hard, the network tells our boat 'take the power' and ultimately as we build up, it tells Belfast Harbour which uses a huge amount of energy 'take that energy'.

"Equally when the wind doesn't blow, it says 'don't use that energy' and what does that mean?

"It means we don't have to shut down windfarms and ultimately lower energy prices," he added.

This is the second project announced from the £30m allocation to the Belfast-Derry Innovation Corridor.

Economy Minister Dr Caoimhe Archibald said: "It will be developing to try and match up the energy supply with the demands of the harbour, which is a really big user.

"We are really world leading in terms of this so it is a really good investment," she added.

It's hoped what is learned in this project could have wider applications across Northern Ireland.

Dr Percy said: "Where the real accelerator value add comes in here, what can be done on that network can be rinse and repeat anywhere else."

"We already have real buy in from Foyle Port and other regions within Northern Ireland," he added.

articles.title: Franklin Graham shares toll of Billy Graham’s time away evangelizing, recalls not recognizing own father
articles.summary: Franklin Graham recalls not recognizing Billy Graham after a six-month Australia trip, revealing the personal toll of his father's global ministry.
articles.body: The Rev. Franklin Graham is opening up about the toll his father Billy Graham's worldwide ministry took on their family, recalling a heartbreaking moment when he failed to recognize his own dad after months apart. "Mama, who's that strange man in the bed with you?" Graham recalled asking his mother after his father returned from a six-month trip to Australia. The evangelical leader shared the memory, which he attributed to his mother, during an interview on Sean Hannity's podcast, "Hang Out with Sean Hannity," describing how his father's extended travels sometimes kept him away from home for months at a time. Graham explained that the trip took place before jet aircraft became commonplace, when reaching Australia required multiple stops which drew out the experience along the way, including lengthy layovers in Hawaii and Fiji. EXCLUSIVE: FRANKLIN GRAHAM VISITS EMERGENCY HOSPITAL TREATING VENEZUELA EARTHQUAKE VICTIMS "You would fly to Hawaii, then you'd stay a couple of days, then you'd fly to Fiji and stay a couple days, and then you're going down to Sydney or Melbourne or wherever you're going," he recalled. "But my father spent all that time in Australia, and so when he came home ... we [his children] just didn't recognize him," he added. Graham said the incident "hurt" his father, whose evangelistic endeavors remained a cornerstone of his life's work. The world-renowned reverend, who spent decades traveling the globe to preach the Gospel, became one of the most influential figures of the 20th century, reaching millions through his evangelistic crusades, television broadcasts and other outreach efforts. articles.title: Syrian court sentences two to death over 2025 coastal violence
articles.summary: Court rulings concern violence and killings during March 2025 uprising by pro-Assad forces and retaliatory attacks.
articles.body:
A court in Syria has sentenced to death two supporters of the ousted Bashar al-Assad regime for inciting an uprising last year, and handed hefty sentences to members of the current government’s security forces for the killing of hundreds of civilians from the Alawite religious minority.

The Military Criminal Court at the Justice Palace in the northern city of Aleppo gave death sentences to Al-Waddah Ismail and Maher Ali, according to state media.

The Syrian Arab News Agency (SANA) reported that the pair were convicted of seeking to incite civil war and sectarian fighting and for leading armed gangs with the intent to attack public forces.

A third defendant, Maher Othman, was sentenced to 12 years in prison, the court also announced on Thursday without immediately specifying the charges on which he was convicted.

In separate rulings, the court sentenced Mohammed Bakour, a member of the Defence Ministry’s 82nd Division in the new government, to 20 years in prison after convicting him of intentional homicide.

It also sentenced Ammar Abdul Aal to three years for torture and acquitted Abdul Raouf Bakrjan and Mohammed Zarzouri, SANA said.

The rulings concern investigations carried out by a government committee into attacks in March last year. At least 1,426 people, mostly civilians, were killed in several days of sectarian violence in the predominantly Alawite areas of Syria’s coastal regions.

The defendants included loyalists to the former al-Assad regime and members of the new government’s security forces. It is the first time government-linked personnel have been put on trial for acts of violence.

The government committee said it had identified 298 suspects implicated in serious violations during the violence in the Alawite heartland.

The committee’s investigation documented “serious violations against civilians on March 7, 8 and 9 [2025], including murder, premeditated murder, looting, destruction and burning of homes, torture and sectarian insults”.

The committee said 238 members of the army and security forces were killed by pro-Assad fighters in the attacks in the provinces of Tartous, Latakia and Hama.

About 200,000 pro-government military reinforcements then converged on the area, carrying out alleged revenge killings.

Al Jazeera’s Heidi Pett, reporting from the Syrian capital, Damascus, said the uprising was started by individuals still loyal to the regime of al-Assad, who himself is from the Alawite religious minority.

“After the Assad regime fell and its leadership fled the country at the end of 2024, supporters including loyal soldiers from the ousted regime as well as militia members fled to the mountains from where they launched an uprising in March 2025 against the new government”, Pett said.

She added that forces loyal to the new government are accused of killing civilians from the Alawite minority group in revenge attacks.

“These trials are for seven men who took part in the initial pro-Assad uprising, and also seven members of the new government’s security forces who were subsequently deployed into the area and are accused of carrying out revenge attacks,” she said.

SANA reported that on September 17, the court issued verdicts in cases involving four other defendants accused of violations during the events in the coastal region last March. One was sentenced to death, one to life imprisonment and one to 20 years in prison; the fourth was acquitted.

articles.title: Man with venomous snakes and lizards stopped at German airport
articles.summary: The man, a Mexican firefighter, looked "nervous" as he tried to leave Cologne Airport, officials say.
articles.body:
A man has been stopped at Cologne Bonn Airport in Germany after trying to smuggle in more than 90 lizards and venomous snakes.

Customs officials said the 45-year-old Mexican firefighter had looked "conspicuously nervous" as he tried to go through the green - nothing to declare - exit at the airport.

They conducted a drugs test on the man - which came back positive for cocaine - before proceeding to check his suitcase.

They did not find any drugs, but vipers, rattlesnakes and other species of snakes and lizards, including iguanas, hidden in shampoo and cream bottles, plastic containers and balls of socks.

"My colleagues at the airport are used to a lot when it comes to souvenirs in suitcases, but we've never had 37 live venomous snakes and 55 lizards from Mexico before," said Jens Ahland, spokesman for the Cologne Customs office.

Some were being kept "in inhumane conditions", Ahland said. Others had died during the journey from Mexico City via Istanbul.

The man, who has not been named, told officers that he had brought the animals back as a favour for a Brazilian acquaintance.

He was denied entry to Germany and flown back to Istanbul.

As for the surviving animals, they are being looked after at a snake farm in Germany.

"Last year, we had over 1,300 seizures nationwide involving more than 56,600 protected animals and plants or products made from them," the Customs spokesman said.

Six years ago, 26 rare reptiles - 10 of them dead - smuggled inside parcels of toys and sweets from Mexico , were found by customs officials at Cologne Bonn Airport.

They were destined for private buyers in Germany.

articles.title: Houthi missile attack on Yemeni presidential palace kills two, minister says
articles.summary: Yemen's information minister says the prime minister and other ministers were unhurt when ballistic missiles hit al-Maashiq Palace.
articles.body:
Two security personnel have been killed in a Houthi missile attack targeting the presidential palace in the port city of Aden in southern Yemen, which is the seat of the internationally recognised government.

The prime minister and other ministers were unhurt when five ballistic missiles hit al-Maashiq Palace, but many others were injured, Information Minister Moammar al-Eryani told the BBC.

Houthi-run media reported that the group had struck "the headquarters of military operations, led by Saudi officers" as well as weapons depots.

A coalition led by Saudi Arabia backs the government and is providing air support for an offensive by pro-government forces against the Iran-backed Houthis.

The Houthis have also launched missiles and drones at airports, oil and gas facilities, and military bases in Saudi Arabia in retaliation for the strikes on the territory that they control in western Yemen, including the capital Sanaa.

On Saturday, a Houthi missile strike killed 13 people at Riyadh's international airport, which was the deadliest attack in Saudi Arabia in more than a decade.

articles.title: US temple attack plot: Teen’s alleged manifesto describes Indians as ‘subhumans’
articles.summary: TOI correspondent from Washington: A malfunctioning rifle stood between a 19-year old white supremacist and his alleged intention to massacre Indians at a
articles.body: TOI correspondent from Washington: A malfunctioning rifle stood between a 19-year old white supremacist and his alleged intention to massacre Indians at a temple near Chicago. Alexandros Paporakis’s plan reportedly came unstuck when his gun got jammed and he contacted a co-worker to say he had escaped “super-fast” and was trying to figure out how to fix the issue so he could carry out the attack later.He subsequently shared electronic messages showing an AR-style rifle failing to fire, along with a photograph of himself wearing a tactical vest.The communications alarmed two colleagues, who then contacted 911. Police from Palatine and neighbouring Mount Prospect coordinated their response and arrested Paporakis as he was leaving his home that afternoon.Local TV footage showed a young man being handcuffed by the police in a parking lot and being taken away. A subsequent search of his residence uncovered an AR-style rifle without a serial number, loaded magazines, hundreds of rounds of ammunition, body armour and items bearing Nazi or white-supremacist imagery.Investigators also recovered a gas canister labelled with a racial slur directed at South Asians, according to prosecutors and police. The FBI, which ironically is led by a MAGA-supporting Indian-American Kash Patel, is reported to be assisting the case.At the centre of the investigation is an eight-page document titled “Why I Fought: A.K.A. (Aurora Shooter’s Manifesto)”. Prosecutors say it denigrated Indians, Jews and African Americans as “subhumans” and described a plan to kill as many people as possible. Paporakis allegedly described himself in the document as a “sociopathic white supremacist Neo Nazi filled with hatred, fantasizing about mass murder nearly every day”.Court documents cited by local broadcasters indicate that the alleged planning had been going on for two years. A judge ordered Paporakis held pending trial; his next court appearance is scheduled for October 30.The case has intensified concerns among Hindu organisations about the safety of temples and worshippers. The Hindu American Foundation (HAF) welcomed the swift law-enforcement response and urged people to remain vigilant and report potential threats, adding that every community deserved to worship without fear.Aurora police also contacted Hindu temples in their jurisdiction after being alerted to the alleged plan. Authorities said they had identified no continuing public threat linked to the case.The episode comes amid mounting anti-Indian hostility in the US, particularly on social media, with immigration and the H-1B visa program increasingly becoming flashpoints. A report by the Centre for the Study of Organised Hate, published in September, found that online anti-South Asian hate had surged, with Indians targeted over immigration status and allegations that foreign workers were taking American jobs.Some community leaders have also spoken about Indians being targeted on account of envy at their success, which was once a matter of admiration but appears to have become a source of resentment in the MAGA era.Surveys show Indian-Americans, by far, rank as the highest-earning and most educated ethnic group in the US, with a median household income exceeding $151,000 and roughly 77% holding a bachelor's or advanced degree.For nearly five million people of Indian origin in the US, the immediate concern is more tangible: whether families can attend a temple, children can participate in religious festivals and communities can gather without fearing that their visibility makes them targets. articles.title: What is the ‘Mother of All Bombs’ US could use in Iran?
articles.summary: US media reports military considering plans to use GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast Bomb (MOAB)
articles.body:
The United States has developed plans to strike Iran with the largest non-nuclear bomb in its military arsenal on Iran’s energy infrastructure and nuclear sites if President Donald Trump orders renewed combat operations, according to US officials cited by CNN.

Deploying the GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast Bomb (MOAB), nicknamed the “mother of all bombs”, could significantly escalate the ongoing conflict at a time when fighting has lulled, experts say.

Concerns are also being raised, including within the Trump administration itself, over what such a move would even achieve. Officials familiar with military planning discussions told US news outlet CNN and Al Jazeera that deploying the MOAB would be unlikely to help the US achieve its stated strategic goals, including to destroy Iran’s nuclear capabilities.

Brussels-based military expert Elijah Magnier told Al Jazeera that using the MOAB would not even guarantee the destruction of Iran’s deeply buried underground nuclear installations and that such a strike would likely amount to little more than “political theatre”.

The GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast Bomb (MOAB) is a massive munition containing about 8,500kg (18,000 pounds or 8.5 tonnes) of high explosives. It weighs 9,800kg (21,605 pounds or nearly 10 tonnes) – about the same as four saloon cars – and is as long as a small yacht at just over 9 metres (about 30 feet).

The MOAB is typically deployed from the Lockheed C-130 Hercules cargo aircraft because it cannot fit in a stealth bomber.

The bomb, which was first manufactured between 2002 and 2003, has undergone 12 detonation tests.

Its name is a reference to former Iraqi President Saddam Hussein’s comments during the 1991 Gulf War when he invoked the “mother of all battles”.

The US has only deployed the MOAB once before – during its 2017 attacks on an Islamic State Khorasan Province (ISKP) cave and tunnel complex in Afghanistan . Afghan authorities claimed that while 94 Islamic State-Khorasan Province (ISKP) fighters were killed in the blast, no civilians were hurt. However, there were unconfirmed, local reports of civilian casualties and many homes were destroyed .

Cradle separates; GPS and fins guide it.

Hot gases, smoke and debris rise in a mushroom cloud.

Designed to explode a few feet above the ground, the MOAB sends out lethal waves of fire when it detonates, blasting away buildings, cave openings and other hard-surface structures.

“Its purpose is to generate an exceptionally powerful blast across a surface area,” Magnier said.

Military expert Colonel Nidal Abu Zeid told Al Jazeera the bomb does not require impact in order to detonate and that its massive blast will destroy everything above ground within a 1km (0.6-mile) radius.

It is likely that the US would aim to use the high-explosive MOAB to completely destroy Iran’s ground-force positions above ground, and to reach its underground facilities, including Pickaxe Mountain, which Trump has previously threatened to attack, Abu Zeid said.

However, Magnier said the bomb’s radius and level of destruction would depend greatly on the terrain it is used within and how populated the area is. He added that it may not be particularly effective against targets buried deep underground.

Some of Iran’s nuclear sites which the US may wish to target, such as the Fordow complex and an under-construction site at the Pickaxe Mountain, are heavily fortified and deeply buried.

“Its large explosive charge can produce devastating blast effects against exposed personnel, equipment and vulnerable structures,” Magnier said. “The Afghanistan operation demonstrates its intended application against a cave-and-tunnel position; it does not demonstrate an ability to destroy every kind of underground installation.”

While its blast can reach underground, the MOAB is not especially designed to punch through deep concrete or mountain rock in the way that a “ bunker buster ” bomb is. The US military’s most powerful bunker buster is the GBU-57 Massive Ordnance Penetrator. Weighing about 30,000 pounds (13,600kg), including a 2,700kg (6,000 pound) warhead, this precision-guided bomb is made of high-strength steel and built to penetrate up to 200 feet (61 metres) underground before exploding.

It already has done – in Afghanistan in 2017.

However, besides not being guaranteed to hit underground targets effectively, Magnier told Al Jazeera it could be difficult to deploy the necessary aircraft in the regions of Iran where nuclear sites are located. Stealth bombers which are better suited to this terrain are not able to carry this size of bomb.

Using the bomb could also destroy infrastructure without inducing Iran to make any concessions, he added, noting that its deployment would risk turning “a spectacular event” into one that ultimately delivers few political results for Washington.

“The question I would put to any commander advocating its use is straightforward: What will this weapon accomplish that another available weapon cannot, and how will that result advance an achievable political settlement?,” Magnier said.

“If the answer centres on the spectacle of the explosion, the proposal is stronger as political theatre than as military strategy,” he added.

CNN reported that Trump, in private discussions, has been seeking a “definitive” end to the war that will prove Washington has been undefeated.

A MOAB strike would likely prompt a major reaction from Iran, experts say, warning that Tehran could even invade its neighbours who host US military assets in response.

Iranian security officials have for months made comments regarding a possible invasion of countries like Kuwait to capture US troops and force Washington to surrender.

In May, during a pause in hostilities, Kuwait alleged that sailors from Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) infiltrated its Bubiyan Island, leading to an exchange of fire between Iranian and Kuwaiti forces. One Kuwaiti was injured and four Iranian soldiers were captured.

Iran denied that it had invaded the island and said the troops’ navigation system had malfunctioned.

On Tuesday, IRGC security adviser Mohammad Reza Naghdi warned that Iran could capture troops if Washington were to launch ground attacks, although military experts have long dismissed Trump’s earlier threats of an invasion due to Iran’s mountainous terrain.

“If the United States launches a ground attack, so many of its troops will be captured that it will be forced to raise the white flag,” he said.

Experts say Iran has been preparing for another round of war by stockpiling weapons, fortifying key nuclear and defence locations, and rallying its supporters.

In a television broadcast on Sunday, National Security Council chief Mohsen Rezaei threatened that Iran would attack regional digital infrastructure , including communication cables, data centres and artificial intelligence facilities in the United Arab Emirates and others, if American strikes resume.

When it comes to self care, taking a long, hot shower is at the top of many people’s list. The steamy atmosphere can feel spa-like and that hot water raining down on you can soothe sore muscles instantly. To find out how hot showers impact your skin, I spoke with two board-certified dermatologists. I also asked them how to determine how hot is too hot and rounded up products that can help you maintain (and regain) the health of your skin. Are hot showers bad for your skin? According to experts, hot showers are not great for your skin. Hot water strips your skin of moisture content and breaks down its natural barrier function. “Our skin barrier is important because it keeps moisture in and protects us from potential allergens and irritants in the outside environment,” says Dr. Caren Campbell, a San Francisco-based board-certified dermatologist at Caren Campbell MD. “If we impair this barrier, too much moisture gets out and allergens and irritants get in, which leads to dry skin, rashes, irritation and potential increased risk for developing allergies.” Here’s the thing: A one-off hot shower here and there probably won’t wreck your skin. But if you consistently take them, it’s likely drying out your complexion. The length of your shower also contributes to how it affects your skin, according to Campbell. The longer your skin is exposed to hot water, the larger the impact will be. In fact, consider using soap sparingly when showering if your skin is already feeling dry because it can strip away natural oils and make it even more dry. “Limit soap to face, underarms and groin unless you are dirty in other places and use a fragrance free gentle soap like the Vanicream Wash,” says Campbell.If you really can’t give up your hot showers, you should focus on rehydrating skin to prevent irritation. “Moisturizing immediately after you finish helps to trap the moisture that enters your skin in the shower and keeps it hydrated,” says Dr. David Rayhan, a board certified dermatologist at Rayhan Dermatology. “This may help avoid dry skin, itching, worsening eczema, and the temporary but harmful effects on your skin’s appearance.” Want more from NBC Selected? articles.title: For more than 50 years, Austinites fought to protect historic Lions Municipal Golf Course from development; now a proposed deal would transfer its 141 acres to the city while UT develops 190 acres nearby
articles.summary: For more than half a century, Austin residents have fought to protect the historic Lions Municipal Golf Course from being taken over by property
articles.body: For more than half a century, Austin residents have fought to protect the historic Lions Municipal Golf Course from being taken over by property developers. Now, a proposed agreement between the City of Austin and The University of Texas at Austin (UT) would transfer full ownership of the 141-acre golf course to the city, protecting the historic green space for the future. Under the deal, the university would receive updated rules for developing about 190 acres of nearby land it owns along Lake Austin Boulevard. The agreement could end a long-running dispute over the future of the course, known affectionately to locals as Muny. It sits on valuable waterfront land near downtown Austin.Transferring ownership of a civil rights landmarkMuny opened in 1924 on land owned by the university system along Lady Bird Lake. The City of Austin took over the lease in 1937 and has run the course as a public golf facility ever since. The course is popular with local golfers, but it also holds an important place in history. In 1950, Muny became the first public golf course in the southern United States to integrate. It allowed African American players to use the course before courts ordered desegregation. This historic decision helped the site earn a place on the National Register of Historic Places. "This is a great day for Austin," said Austin Mayor Kirk Watson in an official statement released by the city on 14 October 2026. "Our community has been working for more than 50 years to save Muny. That work and our strong partnership with the University have paid off and now we will be able to preserve this precious greenspace and a key part of not only Austin's history, but the entire country's." The course remains Austin's busiest municipal golf facility. It hosts more than 75,000 rounds of golf each year, surrounded by historic oak trees.Updating the land agreementThe proposed deal will make formal changes to the 1989 Brackenridge Development Agreement. This agreement is a contract between local government bodies that sets rules for how the university system can develop its land along Lake Austin Boulevard. In exchange for transferring the 141-acre golf course to the city, the city and university will agree on a development plan for the university's remaining 190 acres in the area. This land includes the nearby Brackenridge Field Laboratory and surrounding properties. According to the official announcement published by the City of Austin, the updated agreement also includes several related city actions. These include changing UT's long-term lease for city-owned property at the former Mueller airport site, exchanging certain public rights-of-way, and creating a Tax Increment Reinvestment Zone (TIRZ) to help pay for infrastructure and public improvements across the development area. The land deal would allow the university to move ahead with planned commercial and residential development on its remaining properties. At the same time, it would ensure that the golf course stays intact as open public space.Guiding development along the waterfrontCity leaders said the agreement balances the need to protect public green space with plans for careful urban growth along the sensitive waterfront of Lady Bird Lake. "Development in this special area, along Lady Bird Lake, must be thoughtful and executed with the deepest care," said Austin City Manager T.C. Broadnax in an official statement. "The agreement will enable both the City and the University to guide development in a way that accomplishes each of our goals." Preservation groups, neighborhood associations, and local golfers have spent decades campaigning to stop commercial development at the course. Over the years, supporters formed nonprofit groups, raised money, and contacted state lawmakers and university regents to find a permanent way to protect the land.Timeline for final approvalThe legal process for transferring the land will move through public city procedures over the coming months. City staff are scheduled to explain the proposal to Austin's Environmental Commission and Planning Commission during October. The updated Brackenridge Development Agreement will then go before the Austin City Council for a formal vote on 19 November 2026. After that first vote, city staff and university representatives will spend the winter preparing the detailed development plan and working out the financial structure for the Tax Increment Reinvestment Zone. These remaining details will be reviewed by municipal boards before returning to the City Council for final approval in the spring of 2027. This would complete the legal transfer of the golf course land to the city.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: University of Maryland club tennis team apologizes for sharing ‘abhorrent’ racist imagery
articles.summary: The club tennis team at the University of Maryland apologized for sending a racist graphic as a part of materials for an upcoming tournament at the school.
articles.body: The club tennis team at the University of Maryland apologized for sending a racist graphic as a part of materials for an upcoming tournament at the school. “Last weekend, our club shared an abhorrent image which was included in a tournament program and distributed to teams from the visiting universities,” the team’s apology, which was posted to their Instagram page, began. “We deeply regret sharing this image and the pain this caused as a result of our actions.” The team said it has already apologized in person to each of the affected teams, and then followed up with an emailed apology to each of the teams’ captains. But, “a public apology is warranted when the impact of our actions extends beyond those who received the tournament program directly,” the statement said. The Maryland club tennis team forfeited its matches in the tournament over the weekend as a result, which continued for all other participating teams. “Although we did not intend to share an image evoking hate and racism, we take full responsibility for failing to identify and remove it,” the apology said. “We understand this was unacceptable and does not reflect the values of our club.” It remains unclear how that graphic got into the tournament materials and which students on the team are responsible. One of the teams that received the materials was Howard University’s club tennis team. Their team’s president, Toni Rachal, described the graphic in an Instagram statement. The graphic included “a recognizable symbol associated with the Ku Klux Klan (KKK) on the first page” below the Maryland club tennis logo, the statement said. “KKK pointed hood masks complete with eye holes appear in the top right and lower left quadrants, replacing the Crossland coat of arms of the official Maryland state flag,” the Howard club team statement said. “The imagery is a recognizable symbol of white supremacy, organized hate, and violence.” Howard’s team shared an image of the graphic Tuesday on Instagram, writing in the caption that it is “important for people to see what is being condemned.” UMD Recreation and Wellness, which oversees the club team, said in a statement Tuesday that the school learned about the graphic in the tournament materials on Saturday and has since suspended the team pending an investigation. The statement added that although the incident may have involved only a few team members, the school still chose to suspend the entire team until the Office of Student Conduct completes its investigation. The matter was also referred to police, and the University of Maryland Police Department confirmed that it is investigating but declined to provide more information. In a statement, UMD President Darryll J. Pines said the school “condemned the image in no uncertain terms.” “It was deeply harmful and offensive, and I offer my apology for its detrimental impact on one and all,” Pines wrote. Pines added that the university is “committed to doing all we can to repair the hurt and harm that this has caused, but first we must acknowledge how this incident has impacted our community members who are Black or African American, the Howard Club Tennis team, and our Black students on the Maryland Club Tennis team.” Aniya Baker, Vice President of the Black Student Union, also called on the school to prevent incidents like this from happening again. “Creating a safer and more inclusive campus requires more than reactive disciplinary measures; it requires sustained accountability, intentional engagement, and a genuine commitment to protecting and supporting Black students,” Baker said in a statement Thursday. “The University must demonstrate through its actions that the safety, dignity, and well-being of its Black community are priorities every day, not just when an incident demands public attention.” In it’s statement, the Howard team asked that the Maryland team donate all funds from the weekend tournament to the National Museum of African American History and Culture. The UMD team said it would. “Moving forward, we are committed to engaging in education and training about the history and impact of racism and hate symbols,” the apology statement said. “At the request of the Howard University Club Tennis team, and in a demonstration of our commitment to taking steps to begin repairing the harm we have caused, we have made a donation to the National Museum of African American History and Culture.”

articles.title: DOJ touts hundreds of gun, drug arrests as St Louis surge operation ends: 'Violence is not inevitable'
articles.summary: Operation Show Me Justice yielded 435 arrests, 80 kilos of drugs and 166 illegal firearms as federal agents surged into St. Louis over months.
articles.body: The Department of Justice touted hundreds of arrests as part of its Operation Show Me Justice in St. Louis, Missouri, on Thursday. Beginning in August, the operation included members of the U.S. Marshals Service, ATF, DEA and the St. Louis Police Department, all surging their efforts to target guns, drugs and other crimes in the city. Acting Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter announced the conclusion of the months-long operation alongside Sen. Eric Schmitt, R-Mo. FBI ANNOUNCES 305 ARRESTS, 24 MISSING CHILDREN RECOVERED IN CHICAGO DURING OPERATION NEW DAWN "Through Operation Show Me Justice, the teams have arrested 435 for drug crimes, firearm crimes, other crimes. That includes 412 outstanding warrant arrests. Most of these individuals already had outstanding warrants for arrest. Many of them had multiple," McCotter told reporters at a news conference on Thursday. The operation also yielded 80 kilos of drugs, 166 illegal firearms, six machine gun conversion devices, and over $1 million in seized currency, McCotter said. TRUMP ADMIN LAUNCHES 'SUMMER SURGE' OF FEDS TO MAKE DC SAFEST CITY IN AMERICA AHEAD OF 250TH ANNIVERSARY McCotter went on to urge mayors, city councils and state officials across the country to contact federal authorities to carry out similar operations in their jurisdictions. "The mission here rests on a simple premise, which is we don't have to accept violent crime. It's not something you have to shrug your shoulders at. It is not a fact of life in a city or anywhere else," McCotter said. TRUMP’S LAW-AND-ORDER BLITZ MARKS ONE YEAR WITH EYE-POPPING HAUL OF SUSPECTS, GUNS IN BLUE CITY "I want to say something to all the mayors, the city councils, governors, police chiefs who are out there watching now: Violence is not inevitable. We want to partner with you. We want to work with you. We want to help you," he added. So far, federal authorities have also partnered with state and local law enforcement in Washington, D.C. and Memphis to carry out similar operations. FEDS SEIZE MOUNTAIN OF FENTANYL FROM 'OPEN-AIR DRUG MARKET' IN MASSIVE CRACKDOWN TARGETING GANG CREWS Thursday's news conference comes roughly a week after federal and state authorities in California carried out a massive operation targeting Los Angeles' infamous Skid Row neighborhood. articles.title: Taxi driver given fake cash by customer drove to police station
articles.summary: Nottinghamshire Police called the move a "fantastic piece of work" by the driver.
articles.body:
A man was arrested after a taxi driver who was given fake cash drove the suspect straight to a police station.

Nottinghamshire Police said the driver picked up the suspect from Nottingham Road at 23:30 BST on Tuesday.

When the customer continued to change his route, the taxi driver asked how he would be paying, which is when he was handed a counterfeit £20 note, the force added.

After questioning the customer and being given further fake notes, the driver took him straight to Radford Road police station.

The force said officers also carried out a search of a man's address, where they discovered a "Rambo knife" under his mattress.

It added no further counterfeit cash was recovered, but a cannabis cultivation kit was seized from the address.

A 23-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of using counterfeit currency and possessing an offensive weapon in a private place.

Neighbourhood inspector Liz Gaskin, who covers the Radford area, said: "This was a fantastic piece of work by a Nottingham taxi driver.

"As soon as they noticed the man's suspicious behaviour in the back of the vehicle and saw that the money was fake, they decided the end of his journey would be a night in our custody.

"We were of course happy to help, and following a search of the individual's property uncovered further concerning behaviour, which included taking a dangerous weapon out of circulation."
