articles.title: Teacher Abusali Rahman jailed for six years for upskirting pupils
articles.summary: The former supply teacher also created sexualised AI images of pupils and shared them online.
articles.body:
A former supply teacher has been jailed for six years after taking more than 100 upskirt photographs of schoolgirls, including in his classroom, across Greater Manchester.

Abusali Rahman, 37, from Salford, also used artificial intelligence (AI) to create sexualised fake images from pupils' social media photographs which he shared online.

He pleaded guilty to 21 offences , including taking indecent photographs of children and publishing obscene material.

The court heard 15 girls, aged 13 to 16, were targeted at seven secondary schools in Bolton, Bury and Salford. Police said 12 had been identified.

Rahman, who qualified as a teacher in July 2023 after studying at Manchester Metropolitan University, worked as a supply teacher at 25 schools across north-west England.

The court heard he used an iPhone concealed in his top pocket to secretly photograph pupils during lessons.

He also followed girls walking upstairs to take upskirt photographs at the schools where he worked.

He was caught when the mother of one girl was scrolling on X and came across an image of her daughter in her school uniform next to graphic sexual images.

The court heard one girl whose social media photograph had been used was left embarrassed and "weirded out", while another felt "disgusted and upset".

Jailing Rahman at Bolton Crown Court, Judge Kenderik Horne said his position as a teacher had given him access to pupils and classrooms.

"You abused that trust," the judge told him.

Rahman was also placed on the sex offenders register and given a 20-year Sexual Harm Prevention Order banning him from working in schools.

Rahman used pupils' personal information to find their social media profiles before using artificial intelligence (AI) to create sexualised images of them.

Some of the images were posted on X, where one of his accounts had about 1,000 followers.

The parents or guardians of identified victims and the affected schools have been informed.

As some of the girls were undergoing GCSE exams, detectives left it to individual parents to decide whether to tell their children they had been victims of Rahman's activities.

The Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) said investigators also found electronic files containing female pupils' names and addresses, which Rahman had used to locate photographs of them online.

He also researched how to take photographs without being caught and where to buy spy cameras.

Investigators found searches on his phone relating to creating AI images and possible defences for teachers making images of children, the CPS said.

Rahman was arrested in June 2025 after parents raised concerns about images of pupils circulating on social media.

He was arrested again in December 2025 after police gathered further evidence.

Prosecutor Tom Farr told the court that officers had discovered child sexual abuse material, including 226 category C images, some of which were upskirt photographs taken in classrooms and school corridors.

The CPS said Rahman made no comment during his police interview.

Emma Kehoe, defending, said it was not the prosecution's case that Rahman had become a teacher specifically to target schoolgirls.

"He found himself out of control and unable to stop," she told the court.

Rahman pleaded guilty at Bolton Crown Court in May to 12 counts of taking indecent photographs of children, four of publishing obscene material, three of making indecent images, one of distributing an indecent image and one upskirting offence.

Detective Constable Lisa McGaffin, who investigated the case for Greater Manchester Police, said criminals were exploiting rapid developments in AI technology.

She said the emergence of unregulated platforms made such offending increasingly difficult for police to tackle.

Senior crown prosecutor Alexandra Mann described Rahman's offending as a "gross breach of trust".

She said: "Abusali Rahman abused his position as a teacher to capture images of children without their knowledge in a school environment where they were entitled to feel safe."

An NSPCC spokesperson said Rahman's offending had been deeply distressing for the children and families affected.

The charity said young people contacting its Childline service about indecent images often reported feeling afraid, ashamed and unsure where to turn.

It called for stronger action from technology companies, the government and Ofcom to prevent sexualised deepfake images of children being created and shared.

The BBC has approached the government and Ofcom for comment.

articles.title: Israeli ad-tech firm helped place spyware on Al Jazeera devices
articles.summary: Citizen Lab investigation says dozens of Al Jazeera devices were infected by malware planted through advertisements.
articles.body:
Israeli advertising technology company Discover-Tech helped place spyware on dozens of devices used by Al Jazeera and other companies, a Citizen Lab investigation prompted by Al Jazeera’s initial internal probe has confirmed.

Al Jazeera Media Network on Thursday said it “condemns the targeting of devices belonging to several of its employees with spyware” and pledged to continue to “protect its employees and systems”.

The network said targeting journalists is an “assault on press freedom and the public’s right to knowledge” and called for those responsible to be held accountable.

Spyware from Candiru, an Israeli spyware firm blacklisted by the United States government in 2021 for its malicious cyber activities, was planted on these devices, using what Citizen Lab described as the first-known instance of “zero-click” targeted advertising.

The Citizen Lab, a research unit at the University of Toronto, concluded in its report that Discover-Tech purchased the advertisements with built-in spyware. It then directed devices to Candiru’s malware through these advertisements.

Al Jazeera journalists were among the millions whose devices were targeted – including several who reported on sensitive subjects.

Al Jazeera’s in-house technology team first discovered unusual patterns on devices used by some journalists in 2024. The pattern continued into 2025. Al Jazeera reached out to Citizen Lab for a more detailed investigation into its suspicions that spyware was responsible for the activity.

“Analysis of network logs provided to the Citizen Lab by Al Jazeera collected during the attack period provides a clear temporal signature of how the attack was executed,” the University of Toronto-based team said in its report published Thursday.

Al Jazeera said that the cooperation “contributed to verifying these attacks and publicly documenting them”.

The “zero-click” nature of installing this spyware means that once an infected advertisement appears on a device, that device, too, is infected — spying on, and feeding, all the data and information available on that platform to those stealing it.

Meanwhile, New York-based advertising security firm Confiant said in a separate report that some of Discover-Tech’s advertisements also appeared in critical networks used by the Pentagon, the United Nations International Atomic Energy Agency and the International Criminal Court.

Candiru’s spyware has previously been used to carry out surveillance on at least 100 journalists, dissidents and others in several countries.

articles.title: Governor clears Karnataka Apartment Ownership Act
articles.summary: Karnataka Apartment Ownership Act comes into force after governor’s assent and gazette notification, creating a unified framework for apartment ownership and management statewide.
articles.body: Bengaluru: The long-awaited Karnataka Apartment Ownership Act has finally come into force, with the state govt issuing a gazette notification on Thursday after the legislation received the governor’s assent.The development marks the culmination of a process that began several years ago, driven by persistent demands from apartment owners and resident groups seeking a modern legal framework to govern apartment communities in the state.The bill was passed by the legislature and approved by the state cabinet earlier this year. However, it was subsequently returned by the governor, who sought clarifications from the govt on certain provisions. After the govt submitted its response last week, the governor gave his assent, paving the way for the law to be notified.According to the notification, the Act seeks to consolidate laws relating to apartment ownership, make an individual apartment a heritable and transferable immovable property, and provide a comprehensive framework for the governance and management of apartment complexes across Karnataka.The law also provides for ownership of an individual apartment along with an undivided share and interest in common areas and facilities attached to the property. It aims to establish clear mechanisms for administration, maintenance and use of common areas within apartment communities.The move addresses a long-standing demand of homebuyers and resident welfare groups, many of whom had complained about confusion arising from the existence of multiple laws governing apartment ownership and associations. The issue had also figured in court proceedings, with Karnataka high court previously noting the ambiguity surrounding the legal framework applicable to apartment complexes.The proposal was first announced by the then deputy chief minister, DK Shivakumar, during a Brand Bengaluru interaction with apartment residents in 2023. articles.title: Albania’s PM dismisses calls to resign as student protests spread
articles.summary: Prime Minister Edi Rama condemns ‘chaos’ as protests continue for third day in the capital and spread to other cities.
articles.body:
Albania’s prime minister has dismissed calls for his resignation as thousands of protesters clash with riot police in the capital for the third day in a row, leaving government buildings damaged.

“My responsibility is to listen, address legitimate concerns and keep Albania moving forward,” Prime Minister Edi Rama said in a written statement to the Reuters news agency, following protester demands for him to resign.

“The alternative would be a betrayal of the Albanians who gave me a strong mandate ‌to complete negotiations on European Union membership,” Rama added on Thursday.

This comes as riot police used water cannons and tear gas against crowds of protesters in the capital, Tirana. Demonstrators have accused officials of corruption and neglecting education, ⁠expressing anger about the sale of parts of Albania’s southern coastline to a luxury resort development backed by United States President Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner.

Tirana’s streets were littered with burnt-out rubbish bins, shattered bus stops and broken traffic lights. In the capital’s central Skanderbeg Square, police hit fleeing protesters with batons as tourists looked on.

Thursday’s protests also spread to several smaller cities as students joined university boycotts.

Rama, whose government denies corruption, said he would be ready to discuss rising education costs but rejected the calls to resign.

“Perhaps some forces, at home and abroad, do not want Albania to succeed as a forerunner for EU membership. But I will not allow violence to derail Albania’s European future,” Rama said in his statement to Reuters.

Rama earlier posted a video on his Facebook page showing him touring the burnt-out remains of an office at a university campus in Tirana.

“Until yesterday, this was the office of the College of Europe, the school of a united Europe,” he said in the video, his first public comments since the protests began.

“Everyone is responsible before the law, and everyone who has had a hand in this chaos will certainly pay.”

The prime minister was due to meet his party’s parliamentary group early on Thursday, when protesters circulated an “ultimatum” demanding his resignation by 1pm (11:00 GMT).

But even before the deadline passed, protesters had already begun clashing with police, building makeshift barriers and setting fire to bins.

‘Our prime minister is the meaning of the word corruption’

A student who gave her name as Kiara told Reuters the cost of living, poor job prospects and alleged corruption were the main issues for protesters.

“Our prime minister is the meaning of the word corruption. You can only find work in your field if you know a guy who knows a guy,” she said, her face covered by a mask, like many on the streets on Thursday.

The protesters demanded Rama’s resignation, saying no one had listened to their concerns during a summer of largely peaceful protests over the luxury resort development linked to Kushner .

Police said 65 people were arrested during Wednesday’s protests, suspected of “attacking police officers, institutions, public and private property”.

The Health Ministry said in a statement that hospitals in Tirana treated 89 people on Wednesday, including 61 police officers.

Four officers and two protesters remained hospitalised, with a demonstrator and two officers expected to undergo surgery.

“Attacking institutions, destroying public property and threatening public safety have nothing to do with the legitimate demands of students,” Rama said.
